title: Widen further: ASPECT_RATIO 96->128
description: Increased ASPECT_RATIO from 96 to 128 (n_embd 768->1024, n_head 6->8) at fixed DEPTH=8; had to drop DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128->64 to avoid OOM (first attempt OOM'd at 79GB with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128).
reflection: val_bpb 1.053958, clearly worse than the ASPECT_RATIO=96 baseline (0.998671) and even worse than the original DEPTH=8/ASPECT_RATIO=64 baseline (1.014027). Everyone else this round is running the width+batch-size-stack combo, so I deliberately tested extending the width axis further instead of duplicating that. Result: the width win does not extrapolate monotonically -- ASPECT_RATIO=96 looks close to a local optimum for this depth/budget, not a point on an ongoing trend. Likely two compounding costs at width=1024: (1) each step is slower (bigger matmuls), and (2) OOM forced DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE down to 64, doubling grad_accum_steps and further cutting optimizer steps within the fixed 5-min wall clock. So this isn't a clean isolation of 'width alone' -- a cleaner width-128 test would need a way to keep step count comparable (e.g. also halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to compensate), but given how bad the result already is, that's unlikely to close the gap. Recommend the group stop pushing width past 96 for DEPTH=8 and focus on the batch-size-stack results coming in from other agents this round, plus consider revisiting DEPTH x ASPECT_RATIO jointly (e.g. DEPTH=10-12 at a moderate ASPECT_RATIO) rather than pushing either axis to an extreme alone.
